paper_title: One Tokenizer To Rule Them All Emergent Language Plasticity via   Multilingual Tokenizers
caption: : Effect of vocabulary size.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the effect of vocabulary size on accuracy for two different tokenizers, identified in the legend as "universal" and "cluster." The x-axis lacks an explicit axis label but displays discrete values representing vocabulary size, with categorical tick marks evenly spaced at 100k, 175k, and 250k. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy (%)" and employs a linear scale with a visible range extending just below 40.5 to exactly 42.0, featuring numeric tick labels at regular intervals of 0.5. The "universal" tokenizer is represented by a solid blue line with star-shaped markers. It exhibits a continuous upward trend across the x-axis, starting at an accuracy of approximately 40.45 at 100k, rising to roughly 41.13 at 175k, and concluding at a peak of approximately 41.87 at 250k. The "cluster" tokenizer is depicted by a solid orange line with circular markers. This line begins at an accuracy of approximately 41.62 at 100k, increases slightly to reach a peak of roughly 41.76 at 175k, and then declines to finish at approximately 41.42 at 250k.
